Hey everyone, so I wanted to share my experiences with some of my guns more so I decided to write up my thoughts on the PPS M2 now that I've owned it for awhile.

Background:

I wanted a concealed carry pistol after having to deal with some uppity "teens" awhile back. I subscribe to the philosophy of whatever gun you have on you is better than nothing, kind of like the best camera you have is the one on you, not that awesome DSLR you left at home. So I decided to go with a single stack 9mm that I would be more liable to carry all the time. Speaking with other gun owners, Glock, Walther, and Sig were the top brands recommended for reliability, which was the other primary consideration. I didn't like how the glock 42 handled ergonomically and heard great things about the PPS M2 in that regard, so I picked one up for about $280 + s/h + FFL fees, so about $320 total.

Overall here are my impressions:

Reliability: I've shot about 600 rounds through it now, with one misfeed in the first couple hundred rounds that occurred with Hornady critical defense type ammo. One of the flanges of the bullet got caught in the slide somehow, but it was easy to clear. After that I went back to shooting the cheap winchester 9mm FMJ ammo and haven't had a problem since. I've cleaned it once and it has performed flawlessly, so reliability seems good.

Maintenance: It's a handgun, not that difficult. Very simple to disassemble.

Ergonomics: I love the ergonomics. Even though it's a small, thin, gun it fits very well in my hands. The grips are good and I don't see any point in "upgrading" them. The recoil is very manageable because of this.

Size: Size is good. The grip length is a little longer than something like a glock 42, but you can use the lower capacity magazine for a more similar size. Thinness is good. But overall I almost want something smaller, like a Walther TPH size, for everyday carry. Sure it would have no stopping power, but it would be something I'd always have on me regardless of attire.

Weight: It definitely weighs more than other single stack pistols. I don't mind this at all really.

Accuracy: Good BUT, I'm not a very good pistol shooter and this thing isn't the easiest in the world to shoot. It fits naturally in my hands but it seems like the point of aim is always just a little off of where I feel it should be. I've tried finding a forum thread about this that I read, but after listening to someone else's advice my accuracy greatly improved. So when I'm shooting right it shoots well, but it doesn't seem to be the easiest pistol to shoot accurately (or I'm just bad, which is more likely).

Overall I guess the real test is do I carry this daily? The answer to which is no, I don't carry it daily. It sits in my car. I'm skinny so it sticks out too much in an ankle holster, would show up too much if I put it in my waistband, so I wouldn't really carry it except for in a suit where I could hide it under the baggy pants or in the jacket.
Try getting a good appendix holster or a kydex pocket holster. I carry a sig 365 with a light in my pocket at work and no one knows.

Yeah, my workplace is very gun friendly so no would care, but I want it to be as invisible as possible. I'll try the appendix holster. My coworker recommended that but I'm stubborn and went for an ankle holster.
I can make an appendix holster disappear, but I actually work at work and it can get in the way of you have to bend over.

I daily carry a S&W M&P Shield 9.The model with integrated red laser. The spare mag for it does stay in the car though, as I don't have a place for it in my daily setup.

It looks like the top one in this image.

It has been extremely reliable. I am somewhere near 500 rounds through it, with no misfires or failure to feed. After taking some time to adjust the integrated laser to point of fire, it is really easy to shoot and very accurate.

I am not a big guy at all, 5'9 170#. and it hides decently in appendix carry. I can also carry it in my work pants pocket, docker type casual slacks, with less profile than my phones. No one notices it. Or, at least no one has said they notice it, or even alluded to it.

The worst part about it, is changing the laser battery, and initial laser adjustment.

I did have to buy a second of the extended (1 additional round) mag, in order for it to fit comfortably in my hand. The standard mag leaves my pinky finger under the hand grip, which feels uncomfortable to me.

You just throw it in your pocket? If I put the 6 round mag in the PPS M2 my pinky dangles, but from time on the range it doesn't seem to affect my accuracy much, if at all. So I was kind of thinking about that for daily carry. I'm pretty sure it's too big for pocket carry though, unless I put it in my jacket pocket.

Yeah, I made sure to buy the model with the actual safety (they are sold with both real safety, and only trigger safety (think glock safety)) specifically for that reason, so I wouldn't have to holster it in clothes where that may be a problem.

The safety sits nicely under my thumb for ease of use.

Granted I've never actually had a situation that called for me to use it, but i am sure I could, as I practice removing it from my pants pocket and triggering the safety and laser.
